rules.statement: Do not let a frontend test pass while it logs console.error or console.warn; fix the cause (for example an unsettled async update producing a React act(...) warning), and when logging is the behavior under test, mock the method with vi.spyOn(console, ...).mockImplementation(...) and assert on the spy.
rules.why: Console warnings during tests show a test asserting before async work has settled, so it can pass for the wrong reason, and new warnings get lost among old ones.
rules.check: Look for tests that are expected to trigger console output without a local spy and an assertion on it, and for changes that silence or filter console output globally instead of fixing it.

rules.statement: Add a message to the fail-on-console exemption list only when it is a timing diagnostic that depends on machine load, never a warning that reflects a code defect.
rules.why: Exemptions exist only for messages whose firing depends on load and not on code (such as Redux Toolkit's slow-check notice); exempting real warnings brings back the noise the guard removes.
rules.check: Look for new entries in the console-guard ignore list and ask whether each is purely a timing diagnostic.

rules.statement: Every frontend workspace's lint script must pass --max-warnings 0, and the ESLint config must report unused disable directives and unused inline configs as errors.
rules.why: Without this, lint warnings and stale eslint-disable comments pile up unnoticed.
rules.check: In a package.json lint script or eslint config, look for a missing or nonzero --max-warnings, or for reportUnusedDisableDirectives being relaxed.

rules.statement: Every Vitest configuration must set expect.requireAssertions so a test that makes no assertion fails.
rules.why: A test shouldn't be able to pass just by running code without checking anything.
rules.check: Look for a new or changed Vitest config or preset that omits or disables expect.requireAssertions.

rules.statement: Frontend tsconfig files must not exclude test files (*.test.*) or Storybook stories (*.stories.*), and must include the Vitest setup file, so they are all type-checked.
rules.why: Vitest strips types without checking them, so a type error in an excluded test or story never fails anything.
rules.check: Look for tsconfig exclude patterns that match test or story files, or include lists that leave out vitest.setup.ts.

rules.statement: Coverage include patterns must cover all .ts and .tsx sources, excluding only the app entry point (main.ts/main.tsx) and the re-export barrel (index.ts), and test globs must match both .test.ts and .test.tsx.
rules.why: Narrow patterns left whole files out of coverage, and a narrow test glob meant some test files would never run.
rules.check: Look for coverage include/exclude or test include globs that leave out a source extension, a test extension, or source files other than the entry point and barrel.

rules.statement: Each frontend workspace must set coverage.thresholds for statements, branches, functions and lines at its achieved level rounded down; a change that raises coverage raises the floor in the same change, and a change that lowers a floor must state why.
rules.why: Floors stop coverage regressions in CI instead of leaving them to be noticed later in Codecov.
rules.check: Look for coverage gains without a matching threshold bump, threshold reductions without a stated reason, or workspaces with no thresholds.

rules.statement: Do not raise a build warning limit (such as Vite's chunk size warning) to silence a warning; fix the underlying cause instead.
rules.why: Raising the limit only hides the problem the warning reports.
rules.check: Look for config changes that increase chunkSizeWarningLimit or similar thresholds just to make a warning go away.

rules.statement: Client code must treat an access token as opaque and must never parse it to get user identity or claims; get user information from the ID token or the userinfo endpoint instead.
rules.why: Parsing the access token broke sign-in and renewal when the token was opaque.
rules.check: Look for client code that decodes or splits an access token (for example base64-decoding its payload) to read claims.
